7331c9e36b.q: What is the Free Lunch Metric used by real estate investors to evaluate property quality?
7331c9e36b.a: The Free Lunch Metric uses the percentage of students qualifying for free lunch in a local school district as a proxy for neighborhood quality. David Porter established a threshold of 50 percent: if more than 50 percent of local students qualified for free lunch, he would not invest in that area. He linked data from Zillow to greatschools.com to identify this metric and used it consistently across all his property purchases without ever violating this rule.

76f3ab0794.q: What maximum insurance deductible strategy does David Porter recommend for rental properties?
76f3ab0794.a: David Porter switched to a maximum deductible strategy on all his rental property insurance, with deductibles ranging from $5,000 to $10,000 depending on the carrier and market. He adopted this approach to insure against catastrophic loss only, avoiding small claims that would trigger rate increases, and successfully reduced his overall insurance costs while never filing a claim across all his years as an investor.
